b1-conquista-01.title: Communicative Challenge: The Noche Triste
b1-conquista-01.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos have watched a documentary about the fall of Tenochtitlan, and he asks what happened to the Spaniards during the Noche Triste.
b1-conquista-01.prompt: Tell Carlos what happened to the Spaniards in June 1520.
cues: Say that the Spaniards were expelled from the city
Say that many of them died
b1-conquista-01.target: Los españoles fueron expulsados de la ciudad y muchos murieron.
b1-conquista-01.english: The Spaniards were expelled from the city and many of them died.
b1-conquista-01.canDo: I can use the passive with *ser* to tell what happened to the Spaniards and to Tenochtitlan.

b1-conquista-02.title: Communicative Challenge: When Pizarro Arrived
b1-conquista-02.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are reading a book about Pizarro, and she asks what state the Inca empire was in when he arrived.
b1-conquista-02.prompt: Tell Meg what had already happened to the empire when Pizarro arrived.
cues: Say that a war between two brothers had already divided the empire
b1-conquista-02.target: Cuando Pizarro llegó, una guerra entre dos hermanos ya había dividido el imperio.
b1-conquista-02.english: When Pizarro arrived, a war between two brothers had already divided the empire.
b1-conquista-02.canDo: I can use the pluperfect to say what had already happened before another moment in the past.

b1-conquista-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Why Tlaxcala Joined Cortés
b1-conquista-03.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are visiting a museum exhibition about the conquest, and he asks why the Tlaxcalans joined Cortés.
b1-conquista-03.prompt: Tell Carlos why the Tlaxcalans joined Cortés.
cues: Start with a gerund that says what they hoped
b1-conquista-03.target: Esperando liberarse de los mexicas, los tlaxcaltecas se unieron a Cortés.
b1-conquista-03.english: Hoping to free themselves from the Mexica, the Tlaxcalans joined Cortés.
b1-conquista-03.canDo: I can use the gerund to say how or why someone acted.

b1-conquista-04.title: Communicative Challenge: What Las Casas Asks
b1-conquista-04.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are talking about a class on Las Casas, and she asks what he wanted from the king.
b1-conquista-04.prompt: Tell Meg what Las Casas asks the king to do.
cues: Say that Las Casas asks the king for something
Say who the king should protect
b1-conquista-04.target: Las Casas pide al rey que proteja a los indígenas.
b1-conquista-04.english: Las Casas asks the king to protect the indigenous people.
b1-conquista-04.canDo: I can use *pedir que* and *querer que* with the subjunctive to say what people ask others to do.

b1-conquista-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Conquest or Catastrophe?
b1-conquista-05.scenario: You are Meg. You and Carlos are talking about a book on the conquest, and he asks whether historians think conquest is the right word.
b1-conquista-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what some historians think about the word conquest.
cues: Say that some historians believe conquest is the right word
Say that others do not believe it explains everything
b1-conquista-05.target: Algunos historiadores creen que conquista es la palabra correcta, pero otros no creen que explique todo.
b1-conquista-05.english: Some historians believe that conquest is the right word, but others do not believe that it explains everything.
b1-conquista-05.canDo: I can use *creer que* and *no creer que* with the right mood to say what historians think.

b1-conquista-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Summing Up the Conquest of Peru
b1-conquista-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. You and Meg are preparing for a class on the conquest, and she asks you to sum up what happened in Peru.
b1-conquista-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg how the conquest of Peru began.
cues: Say that a war had already divided the empire when Pizarro arrived
Say that Atahualpa was captured at Cajamarca
b1-conquista-consolidation.target: Cuando Pizarro llegó, una guerra ya había dividido el imperio, y Atahualpa fue capturado en Cajamarca.
b1-conquista-consolidation.english: When Pizarro arrived, a war had already divided the empire, and Atahualpa was captured at Cajamarca.
b1-conquista-consolidation.canDo: I can talk about the conquest of Mexico and Peru with the passive, the pluperfect, the gerund, the subjunctive after requests and *creer que*.
